newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar jumps on consumer buying, speculation.
newsitem.headline: India sugar jumps on consumer buying, speculation.

text.p: Sugar prices jumped up on the local market on Monday, dealers said.
Fresh consumer buying lifted prices while reports of lower allotment of sugar to states prompted speculative interest.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 18/20 rupees to 1,458/1,490 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose by 5/10 rupees to 1,475/1,515 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery also rose by 20/30 rupees to 1,415/1,420 rupees per quintal for the S-30 variety and to 1,425/1,450 rupees per quintal for the M-30 variety.

The federal government has allocated 1,902,536 quintals of sugar to Maharashtra state out of the total Indian free sale quota of 750,000 tonnes for July. In June, this allotment was higher at 2,366,029 quintals out of the total Indian quota of 800,000 tonnes.
"The month is over and we are expecting higher demand in coming days," a broker said.
